Agent-authored (Claude). Play both could only press keys, so a mouse behavior could not be compared. Request #1202 is one: "a click outside closes the list and keeps the highlighted option picked". This PR adds one pointer gesture. It does not change any component's docs. On main, Select's `close-on-outside-click` has no keys. Adding the gesture to a behavior is the preview branch's job.

**Stacked on #1207.** Both PRs change the same lines of `.storybook/preview.tsx`. When #1207 merges, GitHub moves this PR's base to `main`.

- `@bridge-ds/core`: the `ComponentBehavior.keys` doc comment now lists the token `click-outside`, and `CLICK_OUTSIDE` is a new export. `keyLabel('click-outside')` returns "Click outside", which is what the Studio and Library `Kbd` show. The behavior-preview brief now tells Claude to write a click away from the component as `click-outside`, so Studio can replay it. docs.json has no JSON schema: the TS type and `validateBehaviors` act as the schema, and the validator already accepts the token.
- `.storybook/preview.tsx` (`embed=bridge-keys`): `click-outside` runs `userEvent.click` on a small spot added for this (fixed, 8 by 8, bottom-right corner, `aria-hidden`). The spot sits outside the story root and outside every portaled popup. It is created **before** any key is pressed. In real Chrome, a spot added after the Select popup opened was ignored and the list stayed open, because floating-ui treats elements added after the popup opened as third-party overlays. The result line already reports what the control shows.
- `replaySequence` needs no change. A behavior with `keys: ["click-outside"]` plays the opening key, then a move, then the click (`Enter, ArrowDown, click-outside` on Select).

Real-browser check: playwright-core with Chrome, the same `userEvent` that the Storybook build exposes, on the live Storybooks, `forms-select--default`, keys Enter, ArrowDown, click-outside, 4 runs per side:

body.title: Studio: Patterns page under Design system, after Components
body.body:
## What changed and why

Adds **Patterns** to the Studio rail, under Design system right after Components (icon `hand`), and the Studio page behind it (`/studio/patterns/`, team shell `/studio/<owner>/<repo>/patterns/`). Agent-authored (Claude), following the brief for the Studio side of Patterns (Library side: #1174; behavior requests: #1179 to #1182).

**The page**: one sentence ("3 interactions and 2 actions shared across the product."), then one DS Table with the kinds as quiet row-group labels, Interactions then Actions, same order as the Library. Each row: the pattern name linked to its Library page, what it is for, the components it uses. Everything comes from `patterns/<id>.pattern.json` through `libraryPatterns(model)`; nothing is invented. No pattern: a DS EmptyState, and the header sentence stays empty so the state is said once.

**Changes asked on a pattern**: only for whoever decides on behavior requests (a library reviewer or a design lead, the same check as Home's Decide rows), the page reads the open `request: behavior` issues once and adds a "Waiting for your decision" column, only when at least one waits. A request concerns a pattern when its Bridge block asks about it (`behavior.of: 'pattern'`), or asks about a component behavior whose id is an interaction pattern (`Select` + `close-on-escape`). Like Home, it leaves out requests already made the default (`bridge-build`, on Being built) and requests someone is assigned to. Each request links to its request page (`explorations/?request=N`).

**Nav gating**:
- Bridge's own Studio lists the entry while `patterns/` has some (built in `studioNav()`).
- A team's Studio builds it hidden (`until: 'patterns'`, like the team Library). It shows once the team's data has patterns. `loadTeamData()` notes the answer per team in localStorage (`bridge.nav.patterns:<team>`) and fires `bridge:team-patterns`. The rail paints from that memory on the next pages and reads the team data only when the browser never saw this team. That read is memoized per page and shared with the page's own read.
- Not `branchAware`: the page reads the latest library only, so a "Viewing" selector there would change nothing.

Also: Studio search lists Patterns, `patterns/` is a team shell route, and the total-length cap in `nav.test.ts` now allows the Design system group (top-level still capped at 7, group at 4).

## Risk tier

- [x] Tier 1, low: docs-site page and nav entry, no DS component, prop or token change
- [ ] Tier 2, medium
- [ ] Tier 3, high

## Authored by

- [ ] Human
- [x] AI agent (Claude), reviewed by a human before merge

## Design review checklist

- [x] Uses tokens only (`stylelint` passes on `studio-patterns.css`)
- [x] Semantic tokens only
- [ ] Checked in light and dark: desktop light screenshots only
- [x] No axe violations on the table (StudioPatterns.test.ts)
- [x] Changeset added (`@bridge-ds/docs-site` minor)
- [x] No lint rule disabled, no test or story deleted
- [ ] Screens comment reviewed: mobile and dark not checked locally

**UI quality bar**: one summary sentence first, and the column of changes asked appears only for the person who decides and only when something waits (progressive disclosure, actionable only). The group label gives the kind once and rows never repeat it. Only real DS parts are used: Table, Link, EmptyState, SidebarNavItem. No primary action: nothing on this page is the one next step.

## Screenshots

Desktop, light, signed out (so no requests column):
- Bridge's own Studio: 5 patterns, 3 interactions + 2 actions, rail shows Patterns after Components.
- Sample team (acme-design-demo/bridge-demo-ds), read live from the repository: 3 interactions, rail shows Patterns once the data is read.
- Sample team read from its published snapshot: empty state, no Patterns in the rail (see note).

**Note on the sample team**: its `bridge-data` snapshot (written by `bridge` CLI 0.21.2 at 0fcdb26) has no `patterns/` files. A signed-out visitor therefore sees no Patterns until a CLI release that records patterns writes a new snapshot. The team's Library has the same gap today.

## Tests

- `vitest --project docs`: 5276 passed. The only failures come from the local setup (`stripe` is not installed here: billing.test.ts). The one real failure (studio-search pages out of step with the rail) is fixed in this PR.
- `tsc -p apps/docs-site`: clean apart from the same missing `stripe` module.

body.title: fix(figma-plugin): MVP scope, truthful listing, demo script
body.body:
Figma is reviewing DS Bridge (plugin 1693034743850648023) and asked for a demo video. The listing we submitted promised more than the plugin should show. This PR puts the plugin on the MVP scope decided on 2026-11-11 (Studio canvas "Décisions") and 2026-11-10, rewrites the listing around its one promise, and adds the demo script.

**The promise:** "Your tokens sync both ways. Bridge tells you what is missing in your Figma and checks that it has caught up with the code."

## Plugin

- `src/shared/scope.ts`: `PLUGIN_MVP_SCOPE = true`. Hidden behind it (code kept, one edit turns it back on):
  - drawing and updating component sets from code (Include components, Update, Update all);
  - two-way variant sync and component changes sent from Figma (requests, library branches, Request a component change, Not in the design system yet, Fix in Figma first);
  - Ask Claude to fix it / fix all, Claude's fixes and their approval (no `/api/fix-sessions`, no can-approve-fixes call);
  - Draft with Claude and the Claude card in Settings.
- Shown: Sign in with Bridge, Pull of tokens, Push of variable edits (PR or suggestion, contrast), Compare with code, and a new "Components" group on Pull: "0 of N components from the code are in this file" with the missing ones by name.
- "Send to Figma" is a Studio button, already off (`SEND_TO_FIGMA_IN_STUDIO`); the plugin has none.
- `manifest.json`: name **DS Bridge** (id unchanged), `bridge.floriangouloubi.com` removed from `allowedDomains` (never fetched; links still recognised), reasoning lists only what the MVP calls (`/api/plugin-link`, `/api/ship`). Window title **DS Bridge**.
- UI copy: the token is "saved on this computer only ... sent only to GitHub and Bridge".

## Docs and listing

- `community/listing.md`: Scope section, new tagline "Your tokens sync both ways between GitHub and Figma." (52/60), description, 12 tags, data security answers, claim-to-code table, what the old copy got wrong.
- `community/demo-script.md`: 9 shots, about 80 s, on `acme-design-demo/bridge-demo-ds`; reply to Figma support.
- README: Scope section, hidden sections marked, Network section, Push step (ready-for-review PR, shipping through Bridge).
- Gallery tooling: `plugin-shots.mjs` reads GitHub anonymously when no token is set and caches answers, waits on the current progress UI; art copy follows the promise; gallery 2 uses PR #468.

## Tests

- `test/flow-mvp-scope.test.ts`: the MVP screens (nothing built, no component scan, no request line, no Draft with Claude, no Claude card, no fix-session read). The flow tests of the hidden features open the plugin with `fullScope: true`.
- `npm test -w apps/figma-plugin`: 322 passed. `npm run plugin:build`: OK.

## What is missing in Figma, by name

A code component counts as in Figma when a set Bridge drew carries its mark, or else when a local component set or lone component has the same name after normalisation ("Forms/Select" is Select; case, spaces, hyphens, underscores ignored). The mark wins. Library components are not counted (the Plugin API cannot list them). Compare with code lists name-only components with "Bridge can't compare this one yet: it was not drawn by Bridge." Nothing is redrawn. Tests: `figma-names.test.ts`, `flow-missing-by-name.test.ts`; 326 passed.

An action appears here once people do the same task the same way in at least two places, like Delete." / "None yet. An interaction appears here once two components do the same thing the same way, like closing on Escape." Fixes the team page having no h1 in that case. |

| Studio drawer | `?suggest=action|interaction|pattern` opens Suggest a pattern once on that kind for a viewer who can suggest, then the address forgets it. Ignored for readers. | |

Copy lives in `lib/library/patterns.ts` (`PATTERN_KIND_EMPTY`, `PATTERNS_EMPTY`, `PATTERN_KIND_SUGGEST`), used by both Library and Studio.

**Nav always shows Patterns** (decision on this PR, second commit): the Library group and the Studio entry show for every design system, even with no pattern, so the empty states are reachable. The `until: 'patterns'` gating is removed (NavEntry/LibraryPage `until`, Layout hidden + data-nav-until, showPatternsNav, ProductsNav's per-team memory: lib/nav-patterns.ts and the bridge:team-patterns event). body.title: Behaviors for overlays and disclosure: 12 shared interactions
body.body:
## What changed and why

Agent-authored (Claude). Overlay and disclosure components now declare their `behaviors` in docs.json, so the shared ids turn into interactions. Before this PR only Select and Combobox declared behaviors, and Bridge had 3 interactions. With this PR there are 12. Every behavior is something the component already does through our wrapper and Base UI 1.9. Each one has a test in `Name.test.tsx` that presses its keys, or performs the click outside. The only exception is Drawer's swipe, which jsdom cannot play (see below).

An overlay's docs `preview` is only its trigger button. Each overlay behavior therefore carries an `example`: the real component (trigger plus content). The live stage on Bridge's own Library can then do what the `try` line says. The `preview` is unchanged, so thumbnails stay the same; AlertDialog's lone danger button is still calmed. One small docs-site change: the example registry now hands `Tooltip` its single trigger element. Example children always arrive as a list, and Tooltip needs one element.

### Behaviors per component (evidence)

- **Dialog**: open-from-trigger (Enter, Space), scroll-lock, trap-focus (Tab), close-on-escape, close-on-outside-click (click-outside; off with `disablePointerDismissal`), focus-on-open, focus-after-close. Tests: Space opens; Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside; a body click closes it, and with `disablePointerDismissal` it does not; `data-base-ui-scroll-locked` is on `<html>` while open; the existing Enter/Escape/focus-return tests.
- **AlertDialog**: open-from-trigger, scroll-lock, trap-focus (Cancel and confirm only), close-on-escape ("Escape cancels", onConfirm not called), stay-open-on-outside-click (own id), focus-on-open (Cancel, or the field with `confirmText`), focus-after-close. All covered by the new tests in AlertDialog.test.tsx.
- **Drawer**: open-from-trigger, scroll-lock, trap-focus, close-on-escape, close-on-outside-click, close-on-swipe (own id), focus-on-open (the sheet itself takes the focus first; the test shows it), focus-after-close. close-on-swipe is evidenced by code only: `swipeDirection={SWIPE[side]}` and the Base UI Drawer docs. jsdom cannot swipe.
- **Popover**: open-from-trigger, close-on-escape, close-on-outside-click, focus-on-open, focus-after-close ("Escape puts the focus back", the case the test covers). It is non-modal by default, so no trap and no scroll lock.
- **Menu**: open-list (Enter, Space, ArrowDown), scroll-lock ("unless opened by touch", per Base UI `modal`), move-with-arrows (wraps, `loopFocus`), jump-to-ends (Home, End), type-to-jump, pick-with-enter, close-on-escape, close-on-outside-click, focus-on-open (from the keyboard), focus-after-close. New tests cover Enter/Space opening, Home/End/wrap, typeahead, focus return after Enter, outside click and scroll lock.
- **Tooltip**: show-on-focus, show-on-hover, close-on-escape. These are the existing tests, unchanged.
- **Tabs**: move-with-arrows (Right/Left, wraps), jump-to-ends (`enableHomeAndEndKeys: true` in Base UI TabsList), pick-with-enter (Enter, Space). New tests for Home/End/wrap and for Space.
- **Accordion**: toggle-section (Enter, Space) and one-open-at-a-time. Both are own ids, covered by existing tests. There is no arrow-key behavior: Base UI 1.9 removed roving focus from Accordion.
- **RadioGroup**, **ChoiceCard**: move-with-arrows ("Arrow keys move the choice"). Existing tests cover it.

### Interactions after this PR (components from the loader)

| Interaction | Components |
| --- | --- |
| close-on-escape | AlertDialog, Combobox, Dialog, Drawer, Menu, Popover, Select, Tooltip |
| close-on-outside-click (new) | Dialog, Drawer, Menu, Popover, Select |
| focus-after-close (renamed "Focus after closing") | AlertDialog, Combobox, Dialog, Drawer, Menu, Popover, Select |
| focus-on-open (new) | AlertDialog, Dialog, Drawer, Menu, Popover |
| trap-focus (new) | AlertDialog, Dialog, Drawer |
| jump-to-ends (new) | Menu, Tabs |
| move-with-arrows (new) | ChoiceCard, Menu, RadioGroup, Select, Tabs |
| open-list (new) | Menu, Select |
| open-from-trigger (new) | AlertDialog, Dialog, Drawer, Popover |
| scroll-lock (new) | AlertDialog, Dialog, Drawer, Menu, Select |
| pick-with-enter | Combobox, Menu, Select, Tabs |
| type-to-jump (new) | Menu, Select |

The pattern files hold only id, kind, name and purpose. The purposes of the 3 existing files are widened so they no longer say "list" only.

### Left out on purpose

- SegmentedControl: its link mode moves with Tab, not the arrow keys.
- Slider: its arrow keys change the value, which is not the move-with-arrows meaning.

body.title: Patterns: a Used in place can be in a product's own repository
body.body:
## What changed and why

An action pattern's `usedIn` places could only point at files of the design system repository, so a team whose products live in other repositories (Acme's `crm` -> acme-design-demo/acme-crm, `prints` -> acme-design-demo/acme-prints) could not record where an action really happens.

`PatternUse` gains an optional `product`: a `products[].key` from bridge.config.json.
- Without it, `file` is relative to the design system repository, same as before.
- With it, `file` is relative to that product's repository. A product living in a folder of the DS repo resolves to the DS repo.

```json
{ "screen": "Contacts", "label": "Delete contact", "product": "crm", "file": "src/contacts/ContactRow.tsx", "match": "Delete contact" }
```

- **Core** (`patterns.ts`): `validatePattern` / `readPatterns` / `readPattern` take `{ products }`. An unknown or blank key reports a problem on `usedIn.<i>.product` and the file is left out, the same as any other invalid entry (never dropped silently). `repo-model` passes the config's products. New helpers: `patternUsePlace` and `patternUseHref` (the product repo at `HEAD`, the DS repo at its default branch). `agentPatterns` / `modelAgentPatterns` add `productName` and `repo` to product places, and llms.txt writes `Contacts (Delete contact) in CRM [acme-design-demo/acme-crm]`.
- **MCP**: `bridge_list_patterns` reports unknown keys in `problems`. `bridge_get_pattern` gives `productName` and `repo`, and its tool description says so.
- **Library** (`PatternsView`, Bridge's own page and the team shell): Used in shows "Contacts, in CRM". The "For developers" fold links each file on GitHub, with product files labeled `CRM: src/...`.
- **Bridge's own test** (`packages/core/test/patterns.test.ts`) still checks local files and skips product places, with a comment saying why: it cannot read another repository. It now validates the keys against this repo's products.
- **Docs**: a "Where a pattern happens" section in docs/AI.md, the header comment in patterns.ts, and the behavior build brief (agents writing usedIn add `product` for a place in a product repo).

### Does Acme need a CLI release?

**Not for the Library.** I ran `@bridge-ds/cli@1.0.0` from npm (`bridge snapshot`) on a test repo whose pattern file has a `product` place. The snapshot carries `patterns/<id>.pattern.json` raw, byte for byte, because 1.0.0's validator ignores the extra key and `recordingSource` records the body. The hosted Library runs `loadRepoModel(snapshotSource(snapshot))` with the site's own core, so once this deploys it reads `product`, the product's name and repo, and reports unknown keys. This is covered by a test in repo-model.test.ts.

**A release only matters for two things the CLI computes itself:**
- The published `llms.txt` still writes `Contacts (Delete contact)` without the product until a CLI release.
- `snapshot.json` `problems` won't list an unknown key, but the site recomputes problems from the model anyway.

Nothing was published to npm.

body.title: Studio: Patterns page under Design system, after Components
body.body:
## What changed and why

Adds **Patterns** to the Studio rail, under Design system right after Components (icon `hand`), and the Studio page behind it (`/studio/patterns/`, team shell `/studio/<owner>/<repo>/patterns/`). Agent-authored (Claude), following the brief for the Studio side of Patterns (Library side: #1174; behavior requests: #1179 to #1182).

**The page**: one sentence ("3 interactions and 2 actions shared across the product."), then one DS Table with the kinds as quiet row-group labels, Interactions then Actions, same order as the Library. Each row: the pattern name linked to its Library page, what it is for, the components it uses. Everything comes from `patterns/<id>.pattern.json` through `libraryPatterns(model)`; nothing is invented. No pattern: a DS EmptyState, and the header sentence stays empty so the state is said once.

**Changes asked on a pattern**: only for whoever decides on behavior requests (a library reviewer or a design lead, the same check as Home's Decide rows), the page reads the open `request: behavior` issues once and adds a "Waiting for your decision" column, only when at least one waits. A request concerns a pattern when its Bridge block asks about it (`behavior.of: 'pattern'`), or asks about a component behavior whose id is an interaction pattern (`Select` + `close-on-escape`). Like Home, it leaves out requests already made the default (`bridge-build`, on Being built) and requests someone is assigned to. Each request links to its request page (`explorations/?request=N`).

**Nav gating**:
- Bridge's own Studio lists the entry while `patterns/` has some (built in `studioNav()`).
- A team's Studio builds it hidden (`until: 'patterns'`, like the team Library). It shows once the team's data has patterns. `loadTeamData()` notes the answer per team in localStorage (`bridge.nav.patterns:<team>`) and fires `bridge:team-patterns`. The rail paints from that memory on the next pages and reads the team data only when the browser never saw this team. That read is memoized per page and shared with the page's own read.
- Not `branchAware`: the page reads the latest library only, so a "Viewing" selector there would change nothing.

Also: Studio search lists Patterns, `patterns/` is a team shell route, and the total-length cap in `nav.test.ts` now allows the Design system group (top-level still capped at 7, group at 4).

## Risk tier

- [x] Tier 1, low: docs-site page and nav entry, no DS component, prop or token change
- [ ] Tier 2, medium
- [ ] Tier 3, high

- [ ] Human
- [x] AI agent (Claude), reviewed by a human before merge

## Design review checklist

- [x] Uses tokens only (`stylelint` passes on `studio-patterns.css`)
- [x] Semantic tokens only
- [ ] Checked in light and dark: desktop light screenshots only
- [x] No axe violations on the table (StudioPatterns.test.ts)

**UI quality bar**: one summary sentence first, and the column of changes asked appears only for the person who decides and only when something waits (progressive disclosure, actionable only). The group label gives the kind once and rows never repeat it. Only real DS parts are used: Table, Link, EmptyState, SidebarNavItem. No primary action: nothing on this page is the one next step.

## Screenshots

Desktop, light, signed out (so no requests column):

body.title: fix(figma-plugin): MVP scope, truthful listing, demo script
body.body:
Figma is reviewing DS Bridge (plugin 1693034743850648023) and asked for a demo video. The listing we submitted promised more than the plugin should show. This PR puts the plugin on the MVP scope decided on 2026-11-11 (Studio canvas "Décisions") and 2026-11-10, rewrites the listing around its one promise, and adds the demo script.

**The promise:** "Your tokens sync both ways. Bridge tells you what is missing in your Figma and checks that it has caught up with the code."

## Plugin

- `src/shared/scope.ts`: `PLUGIN_MVP_SCOPE = true`. Hidden behind it (code kept, one edit turns it back on):
  - drawing and updating component sets from code (Include components, Update, Update all);
  - two-way variant sync and component changes sent from Figma (requests, library branches, Request a component change, Not in the design system yet, Fix in Figma first);
  - Ask Claude to fix it / fix all, Claude's fixes and their approval (no `/api/fix-sessions`, no can-approve-fixes call);
  - Draft with Claude and the Claude card in Settings.
- Shown: Sign in with Bridge, Pull of tokens, Push of variable edits (PR or suggestion, contrast), Compare with code, and a new "Components" group on Pull: "0 of N components from the code are in this file" with the missing ones by name.
- "Send to Figma" is a Studio button, already off (`SEND_TO_FIGMA_IN_STUDIO`); the plugin has none.
- `manifest.json`: name **DS Bridge** (id unchanged), `bridge.floriangouloubi.com` removed from `allowedDomains` (never fetched; links still recognised), reasoning lists only what the MVP calls (`/api/plugin-link`, `/api/ship`). Window title **DS Bridge**.
- UI copy: the token is "saved on this computer only ... sent only to GitHub and Bridge".

## Docs and listing

- `community/listing.md`: Scope section, new tagline "Your tokens sync both ways between GitHub and Figma." (52/60), description, 12 tags, data security answers, claim-to-code table, what the old copy got wrong.
- `community/demo-script.md`: 9 shots, about 80 s, on `acme-design-demo/bridge-demo-ds`; reply to Figma support.
- README: Scope section, hidden sections marked, Network section, Push step (ready-for-review PR, shipping through Bridge).
- Gallery tooling: `plugin-shots.mjs` reads GitHub anonymously when no token is set and caches answers, waits on the current progress UI; art copy follows the promise; gallery 2 uses PR #468.

## Tests

- `test/flow-mvp-scope.test.ts`: the MVP screens (nothing built, no component scan, no request line, no Draft with Claude, no Claude card, no fix-session read). The flow tests of the hidden features open the plugin with `fullScope: true`.
- `npm test -w apps/figma-plugin`: 322 passed. `npm run plugin:build`: OK.

## What is missing in Figma, by name

A code component counts as in Figma when a set Bridge drew carries its mark, or else when a local component set or lone component has the same name after normalisation ("Forms/Select" is Select; case, spaces, hyphens, underscores ignored). The mark wins. Library components are not counted (the Plugin API cannot list them). Compare with code lists name-only components with "Bridge can't compare this one yet: it was not drawn by Bridge." Nothing is redrawn. Tests: `figma-names.test.ts`, `flow-missing-by-name.test.ts`; 326 passed.

body.title: Billing with Stripe (test mode, off until launch)
body.body:
**Draft, do not merge.** Ships off: `BILLING_LAUNCHED = false` in `apps/docs-site/src/lib/billing.ts`. With it false, production behaves exactly as today (no Billing card in the page, no Free limit checked, no extra read; billing endpoints answer 503). Flip it on launch day with the pricing page (#1184). Full guide: `docs/BILLING.md`.

## What
- **`stripe` 23.1.0** added to `apps/docs-site` (lock regenerated with `npm install --package-lock-only`).
- **One function, `api/billing`** (`vercel.json` rewrites `/api/billing/<action>`):
  - `GET /api/billing` → `{ billing: 'on' | 'off' }`; `GET /api/billing?team=` (team admin) → the Billing card's status.
  - `POST /api/billing/checkout` (team admin, Free, not founding): Checkout Session, subscription mode, price by lookup key, `automatic_tax`, `tax_id_collection`, `billing_address_collection: required`, customer made once per team and kept, `client_reference_id` = team, back to the team's Settings.
  - `POST /api/billing/portal` (team admin with a customer): Customer Portal session, configuration found by `metadata.bridge_portal`.
  - `POST /api/billing/webhook`: signature checked on the raw body (`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`), idempotent by event id (a failure is forgotten so Stripe's retry runs), handles `checkout.session.completed`, `customer.subscription.created|updated|deleted`, `invoice.paid`, `invoice.payment_failed`; re-reads the subscription from Stripe and stores tier, status, period end, cancel at period end, currency, interval, quantity on the team. Never deletes anything; when it ends, the team is back on the Free rules (founding teams excepted).
  - Without `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` or `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`: "off", every call 503.
- **Quantity**: `min(editors, 10) x design systems (1..3)`, one subscription item (same price per editor on every design system: one invoice line, a design system added later only changes the quantity). A Bridge team is one design system today, so it is the editor count capped at 10.
- **Founding teams**: `bridge:billing:founding:<team>` (`scripts/billing-mark-founding.mjs`, dry run then `--apply`, SET NX), or a team made in Bridge before `BILLING_LAUNCH_DATE`. While that date is null, every team is founding. Never limited, checkout refuses them.
- **Free limits (behind the flag, server side)**: a 4th editor's invite is kept, not emailed, marked "Needs Team" in Members; accepting it, approving a join request, Can view to Can edit, and a Can view invite turned into an editor's answer `409 needs_team`; a 2nd design system (create-team by an admin of a Free team) likewise. Resend sends the waiting invite once there is room. A team made in Bridge keeps its billing when linked to its repository.
- **Studio Settings > Team > Billing** (`BillingCard.tsx`, admins only, not rendered at all while the flag is false): tier and what it includes, founding line, Move to Team with EUR/USD and Yearly/Monthly, quantity and price shown before paying, Manage billing once there is a customer, past-due warning. DS components only (Card, Badge, SegmentedControl, Button, Alert), existing settings classes, no new CSS.
- **Scripts**: `scripts/stripe-catalog.mjs` (products, six prices, portal configuration; idempotent by lookup key; runs in the key's mode), `scripts/stripe-organization.mjs` (customer + yearly subscription, `send_invoice`, `days_until_due: 30`, Stripe Tax; never a second one).

## For Florian
- Vercel env (names only): `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
- Webhook endpoint: `https://bridgedesignsystem.com/api/billing/webhook`, events: `checkout.session.completed`, `customer.subscription.created`, `customer.subscription.updated`, `customer.subscription.deleted`, `invoice.paid`, `invoice.payment_failed`.
- Sandbox: catalog was already there; I created the Customer Portal configuration with the CLI (`metadata.bridge_portal = team`, headline Bridge, privacy `/privacy/`, terms `/pricing/`, invoices, payment method, billing details, cancel at period end without proration, no plan changes). The public business name "Bridge" is an account setting (Dashboard, Public details).
- Launch checklist, E2E test with 4242 4242 4242 4242, and the Organization command: `docs/BILLING.md`.

## Open questions
- Several design systems under one Team subscription: Bridge has no grouping of teams yet (1 team = 1 design system), so each team is billed on its own and the 2nd-design-system limit counts the Free teams an account administers. The quantity formula already takes a design-system count.
- Team quantity is not synced when editors are added later (no automatic charge). Decide: renew at the new count, or a "Update editors" action.
- A waiting invite still expires after 7 days like any invite.
- `/privacy/` must name Stripe as payment processor at launch (in the checklist).

body.title: Behavior requests: Claude's preview, Play both, check against the preview (phase 2, PR 3)
body.body:
Phase 2, PR 3 of 3, on the runner Florian chose: a GitHub Action in the team's repository runs Claude on the request.

## Runner (installed in the team's repo, never ours)
- `packages/core/src/behavior-preview.ts`, `behaviorPreviewWorkflowYaml`: one generator, the same pattern as the automatic measure. It renders `templates/bridge-behavior-preview.yml` (a test keeps the file equal to the generator) and Studio's setup pull request.
- **Trigger**: a `request: behavior` issue opened, edited (her new words) or commented by its requester. An email member's comments count only when they carry her "(via Bridge)" prefix, so the lead's decisions and questions never trigger it.
- **Never runs on**: issues that already carry `bridge-build`, and issues filed by someone outside the team.
- **Run**: Claude Code (`@anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.315`, `-p`, Read/Edit/Write/Glob/Grep only) with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, on `agent/preview-<n>`. It changes the component, its docs.json `behaviors` entry and adds a key-press test. The workflow commits, force-pushes, and opens or updates a draft "Preview for #n" (no "Closes").
- **The comment it keeps**: one sticky comment with `<!-- bridge-preview {...} -->` (preparing, ready with branch/pr/sha/round, failed with the reason, or no-key). Core `parsePreviewState` reads it.
- **Secret missing**: one comment, nothing else runs.

## Play both (request page: the lead who decides and the person who asked only)
- **Today**: the team's published Storybook story. **Claude's preview**: `previews.apps.storybook` for `agent/preview-<n>`. Same story, side by side.
- **Keys**: from the component's docs.json only. The sequence is the Opening behavior's first key, the Moving behavior's first key, then the behavior's own key. They are shown as Kbd.
- **How the keys are pressed**: the frames are cross-origin, so the page sends a postMessage. The story (`.storybook/preview.tsx`, `embed=bridge-keys`) focuses its first control and presses the keys with Storybook's own `userEvent` (`storybook/test`: real keyboard events, Tab moves focus). It posts back the open popup, the focused element and what the control shows.
- **Result**: one line per side, plus "Expected announcement: …" from the docs.json.
- **States**:
  - preparing: "Claude is preparing the preview." It reads again every 30 seconds.
  - failed: the reason, plus "You can still decide on the sentences." for the lead.
  - off: the lead reads one line with a link to Settings, Claude; the person who asked reads nothing.
  - ready, but the team publishes no branch previews: the lead reads that it cannot be played here.
- **G2**: before the decision, the person who asked can use "Change your words". It saves the request (title and body, with the existing path), and the preview reads as preparing until the new one is ready, which says "Updated from your words".

## Check against the preview (Being built, developer, G4)
- Only when Claude's preview is ready and the developer's open pull request has a branch preview.
- Every behavior with keys is played on Claude's preview and on their build, one row each. A row checks when both answers agree; "N of M match", then "Your build does what the preview does."

## Settings, Claude
- New card "Claude's previews", next to the measure: on or off, and whether the Storybook publishes branches.
- The developer fold holds "Turn on Claude's previews" (a pull request adding the workflow), or Open on GitHub and Copy when GitHub refuses workflow writes.
- The secret is named and explained, never asked for.

## Skipped
- G5 (a Base UI update that changes a behavior): it does not fall out of this.
- Being built does not play Today; the check compares the preview and the build only.

## Tests

body.title: Behavior requests in Being built: the developer builds it (phase 2, PR 2)
Le README annonçait MIT, le dépôt est FSL-1.1-MIT
body.body:
## Ce que ça corrige

La page d'accueil du dépôt public annonçait la mauvaise licence, à deux endroits :

- ligne 35 : « Maintained by Florian Gouloubi. **Licensed MIT.** »
- section License : « **MIT**, Copyright (c) 2026 Florian Gouloubi. See `LICENSE`. »

`LICENSE` est la Functional Source License. L'affirmation était donc fausse, et elle se contredisait en citant un fichier qui dit autre chose.

## Pourquoi ça compte

MIT autorise la revente commerciale, FSL ne l'autorise pas pendant deux ans. Un développeur qui lit le README croit pouvoir reprendre Studio et le revendre. C'est la seule protection du modèle, et c'est le seul document que GitHub affiche en arrivant sur le dépôt.

## Ce qui était déjà juste

Le découpage réel est correct partout ailleurs, et il est délibéré :

| | Licence | Fichier `LICENSE` | `package.json` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `react`, `tokens`, `core`, `toolbar`, `eslint-plugin`, `stylelint-plugin` | MIT | MIT ✅ | `"MIT"` ✅ |
| `docs-site`, `admin`, `figma-plugin`, `cli`, `mcp`, `visual` | FSL-1.1-MIT | FSL ✅ | `"FSL-1.1-MIT"` ✅ |

`about.astro`, la FAQ de la page d'accueil, `docs/security.astro` et le pied de page disent déjà « Components and tokens are MIT. Studio, the Figma plugin, the connector and the tools are fair source (FSL-1.1-MIT) ». Rien à corriger de ce côté.

## Ce que fait la PR

Le README porte la carte des deux couches, avec les paquets nommés, et les deux engagements irrévocables : chaque version FSL devient MIT au bout de deux ans, les composants et les tokens restent MIT sans clause de non-concurrence. La formulation reprend celle de `about.astro` et `docs/security.astro`, pour qu'il n'y ait qu'une phrase dans tout le produit.

Aucun code, aucun paquet, aucune licence réelle ne change : seule l'annonce est mise en accord avec les fichiers.

Pas de changeset : aucun paquet publié n'est touché, `changeset status` passe.

Changement écrit par un agent.

body.title: Actions follow the patterns: AlertDialog for what cannot be undone, Undo for the rest
body.body:
Bridge's own screens now follow its Action patterns (patterns/*.pattern.json): a reversible action acts at once with a Toast and Undo; an irreversible one asks in an AlertDialog; high impact adds the typed confirmation (`confirmText`, #1175).

## Changed
| Screen | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Settings, Danger zone: Delete this team / Disconnect this team | Dialog + Input | AlertDialog with `confirmText` (the team's name), refusal said in the dialog |
| Account: Delete my account | inline form, type DELETE | AlertDialog with `confirmText` = the person's **email** (`confirmTextLabel` "Type leo@acme.example to confirm"), after the existing last-admin check |
| Settings, Claude: Remove a connection | no confirmation | plain AlertDialog ("Remove Dana Kim's connection?") |
| Settings, Members: Remove from team | inline confirm row | plain AlertDialog. Re-inviting is a new invite, not an undo, so it asks; not typed: the team keeps the person's work, only their access goes |
| Team chip: Remove from recent teams | silent | acts at once, toast with Undo (puts the list back, same order) |
| Exploration page: Archive | toast, no Undo | toast with Undo (the page's existing Unarchive). A lead archiving someone else's work still writes the reason first: it is a required message to the owner, not a confirmation |
| Branch review: Close change | AlertDialog | acts at once; the repainted review shows "Change closed" with Undo, which runs the existing Reopen and is offered only to who that Reopen allows (author or owner) |
| Token editor review drawer: Discard | `window.confirm` | DS AlertDialog through the new `alertDialogHtml()` of `@bridge-ds/react/dom`, stacked over the static drawer (its scrim covers the drawer: the root is one stacking context on `--layer-modal`) |

`@bridge-ds/react/dom` gets `alertDialogHtml()` / `alertDialogCancel()` / `ALERT_DIALOG_CONFIRM` with a parity test against `<AlertDialogContent>` (a React AlertDialog cannot sit over the static drawer: the DOM focus trap pulls focus back). `scripts/token-editor.ts` lost a dead `#ed-discard` handler (no such element anywhere).

## Left as is (listed, not invented)
- **Remove from Bridge** (product page): reversible (a config change sent for review, nothing deleted, add it again any time), so the typed dialog over-asks, but no take-back of the removal request is wired; needs a decision.
- **Send for review** (integrations, roles, ReviewRulesEditor, ChangesMode, Onboarding, LibraryEditMode, TokenEditorKit, NewBrandFlow, HistoryPlanner, product-branch): no Undo in any of these flows today; the way back exists only on the change page (Back to draft, Close change). Not added.
- **Archive in scripts/explorations.ts** (legacy detail): already acts at once; the repaint puts Unarchive where the button was; no toast host on that page.

## Checks
Targeted vitest (71 files, 1036 tests), tsc for react and docs-site, `tokens:build` + one `astro build`. Screenshots of the Discard AlertDialog over the review drawer from the static build; the other states need sign-in and are covered by component tests (axe where the tests already run it).

body.title: AlertDialog: type the name to confirm when the impact is high; Delete pattern plays both
body.body:
Delete rule (approved): plain confirmation in an AlertDialog; when the impact is high (a team, an account, anything other people lose), the person types the name to confirm.

## AlertDialog
- `confirmText` on `AlertDialogContent` (usually the name of what goes, "Marketing team") adds the DS Input under the description. Optional `confirmTextLabel` (default `Type "<confirmText>" to confirm`).
- The confirm button stays disabled until the typed text matches. Match: outer spaces ignored, case-sensitive (the name as the title shows it).
- Focus starts on the field. Its hint (aria-describedby) says "<confirmLabel> stays off until the text matches."
- Enter in the field confirms only once it matches. The field starts empty each time the dialog opens.
- Without `confirmText` nothing changes (focus on Cancel, confirm on). No new tokens.
- Tests: `AlertDialog.test.tsx` (focus, disabled until match, Enter, reset on reopen, custom label, unchanged plain path, match rule, axe on both states). Story `TypeTheName`. Docs: when to use, do/don't (ask for the name, not DELETE), accessibility, content guidelines, anatomy. `component-specs.json` regenerated (the field part, a "Show confirm text" boolean).
- No `behaviors` list added: the Library's Behaviors stage draws docs.json example nodes and cannot draw an AlertDialog with its trigger, so it would show a dead stage. The Delete pattern stage below plays it live.

## Delete pattern
- Rule: "When the impact is high (a team, an account, anything other people lose), the person types the name to confirm: the AlertDialog's confirmText keeps the delete button off until it matches. Otherwise a plain confirmation."
- Stage: `stage.typeName` names the high impact rows and their question (validated: rows of the stage, not undoable). Rows: Marketing team (typed name, Delete this team), Spring sale draft and Old logo draft (plain, Delete draft).
- "Used in" unchanged and still tested (both real places are high impact; DeleteTeam.tsx and AccountSettings.tsx move to the typed AlertDialog in a follow-up PR).

body.body:
One Library section, **Patterns**, two kinds. Data: one file per pattern in `patterns/<id>.pattern.json`.

### Interactions (derived, not hand-written)
An interaction is keyed by a behavior id of the components' docs.json and exists only while 2+ components list that id. The file holds only `name` and one sentence; the components that do it, and each one's own wording and keys, are read from the components. A test fails when an interaction names an id fewer than 2 components list.
Today: **Close on Escape**, **Pick with Enter**, **Focus after a pick** (Select and Combobox).

### Actions (from an inventory of Bridge's own UI)
- **Delete**: 2 real places (Settings > Danger zone "Delete this team", Account settings "Delete my account").
- **Send for review**: 8 real places; its button reads **Send suggestion** when the team sends suggestions (one verb from `lib/gh-wording.ts sendButton`, so one pattern, not two).
- Every "Used in" place names its file and the text it holds; a unit test checks both exist.
- Rule: Undo in a Toast when it can be undone, an AlertDialog first when it cannot. Places where the code does not follow it are listed below, not changed here.

### Library
- Nav: Patterns > Overview, then each pattern by name under quiet **Interactions** / **Actions** labels (no item repeating "Patterns", no breadcrumb repeating the title).

## What changed and why

Preview of behavior request #1202 for the design system lead to try before deciding. It is a preview, not the build: a developer builds from it or keeps it.

Wanted: "un clic en dehors ferme la liste et garde l'option surlignée choisie".

- `Select.tsx`: when a click outside closes the list, a single Select picks the option highlighted with the arrow keys. Base UI Select has no option for this, so the Select reads the highlighted option when the list closes with the reason `outside-press`. To be able to set the value, a Select that is not controlled now holds its own value (same `value`, `defaultValue` and `onValueChange` API, no new prop).
- `Select.docs.json`: the behavior `close-on-outside-click` becomes `pick-on-outside-click` (the meaning changed), and the keyboard line of the accessibility notes says it.
- `Select.test.tsx`: three tests. Arrow keys then a click outside picks the highlighted option; Escape still picks nothing; a multiple Select only closes.
- `packages/core/test/behaviors.test.ts`: the list of Select behaviors it pins follows the new wording.

Worth knowing before deciding:

- Only a keyboard highlight is kept. Leaving the list with the mouse clears the highlight (Base UI), so a mouse user who clicks away changes nothing.
- Escape and Tab still leave without picking. A disabled option is never picked.
- With `multiple`, a click outside only closes: ticking the highlighted option on the way out would be a surprise.
- `onValueChange` is called once, then `onOpenChange(false)`.

body.title: Spec: Your face, optional drawn-avatar customizer with team-unique Shuffle
body.body:
Draft, docs only (`docs/specs/`). Agent-authored. Risk tier: none (no code); the spec itself flags one Tier 2 (Avatar `xl`) and one optional Tier 3 (tints).

## What this proposes

An optional **Your face** band in Settings > You: one quiet row (your face at 40px + **Change**), opening in place to an 80px preview, **Next to your team** (you and every teammate at 24px), **Shuffle**, and on demand **Pick the parts yourself** (Hair, Glasses, Beard, Expression). Shortcut: "Change your face" in the account menu.

**Uniqueness rule (measured).** At 20px, identity is the hair: hair changes the drawing 0.064, beard and glasses 0.007, eyes/brows/nose/lips 0.001 to 0.002. So within a team a hair style is worn by one person (hard rule, server 409 `face_taken`), and Shuffle also avoids 20px look-alikes (45 measured pairs of 2,016). Whole-face pixel distance alone fails: Dana vs the old Malik drawing measures farther apart than Dana vs Ann. New members get an automatic distinct drawing (`seed#n`), which generalises tonight's `FACE_DRAWING_SEEDS` so nobody writes an exception again. First claim wins across teams; Shuffle avoids taken styles of every team you are in.

**Storage.** A small recipe (part names) on the Bridge account (`POST /api/account { action: 'face' }`, like `aiTools`), plus a per-team face map (`bridge:team:faces:<repo>`) returned by the team read, so `drawFace(seed)` resolves it on every surface. Photo wins over drawing; sample team and no-account sessions keep it in the browser.

**Phases.** P0 no UI (recipe, team map, automatic distinct faces, nightly zero-identical check) fixes the collision alone; P1 row + Shuffle; P2 part pickers + taken states + menu shortcut; P3 photo/drawing choice, tints, phone.
